newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign buying spurs Delhi shares to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying spurs Delhi shares to higher close.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed higher on Monday as strong buying by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) spurred purchases from small investors and speculators, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 6.16 points higher at 738.65.

"Hectic activity in index-weighted shares largely on FIIs buying indicates the market has entered a bull orbit as selling at higher levels was also easily absorbed," said Suresh Aggarwal at brokers Jaimata Securities.

Traders said the begining of a new settlement period on the Delhi bourse coupled with higher Bombay trends also aided the recovery. The Bombay Stock Exchange's sensex closed 34.78 points higher at 3453.10.
"Expectations of a favourable package likely to be announced by the government to revive economy and capital market also fuelled speculative buying," said another broker.
Last week, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda reiterated his commitment to boost industry and speed up economic reforms at an internaional business conference in Calcutta.
He said the government would announce measures to attract more private domestic and foreign investment later this month.
ITC surged 22.05 rupees, or 6.41 percent, to 364.05 on sustained buying by FIIs.
Cement maker ACC was in the spotlight as it rose 65.95 rupees to 1,358.95 on heavy buying by foreign and domestic financial institutions, brokers said.
Reliance Industries ended 2.95 rupees higher at 223.95 on late buying by speculators, they said.
